Civilian Articles

atlases: Human Bodies  ·  Civilian Structures  ·  Civilian Articles  ·  Civilian Outfits

Rendered by game.graphics.expand - the same code the game runs. Nothing here is wired into a playable story yet.

armband

A thin cloth armband on the near upper arm, between the shoulder and elbow. A single free-drawn ring.

armband_medcross

A red medic's armband on the near upper arm with a white cross. Free-drawn ring plus the cross decal.

backpack

A soft-sided backpack worn on the back: the bag itself is drawn behind the torso so only its bulk peeks past the shoulders and sides, while the two shoulder straps show over the front. Free-drawn against the reference body.

badge

A small metal badge of office, worn on the left breast. A single free-drawn shape, tiny enough to sit fine on either body.

bandolier

A single diagonal strap, near shoulder to far hip, strung with three small ammo loops. Same technique as harness, just one strap instead of an X.

belt

A plain leather waist belt with a small metal buckle. Top and bottom edges are the wearer's own waistline and low-waist curves, so it sits flush at the natural waist on any body — no free vertices except the buckle.

braid

A decorative cord looped under the near arm and pinned at the shoulder - an aiguillette. Free-drawn, a thin single shape.

buttons

A double-breasted grid of eight small buttons - two columns of four down the tunic front. Each button is one small octagon; recolour per kit with items/buttons_*.json.

cap

A soft fabric cap, snug over the scalp. Shares hair_short's proven head-fitting silhouette (same coverage, so it sits right without re-deriving head geometry) in cloth instead of hair.

chest_plate

A solid front breastplate, closed edge to edge (no gap, unlike vest/jacket). Same shoulder-arc and side-curve fit as vest, just met at the centreline instead of left open.

collar

A soft folded collar sitting at the base of the neck, worn open over a shirt. Free-drawn against the reference body's neck_base/collar anchors — small enough to read the same on either body.

comms_box

A small comms box clipped to the near side of the helmet, with a single red status indicator. Free-drawn against the reference head - sits the same on either body.

duty_boots

Tall lace-up duty boots, a pair, reaching to mid-shin. Each foot's whole outline is the wearer's own foot curve, so the sole and toe always match; only the shaft above the ankle is free-drawn.

epaulettes

A pair of cloth shoulder boards, one on each shoulder. Free-drawn around the shoulder_near/shoulder_far anchors.

garrison_cap

A soft garrison (side) cap - a creased fore-and-aft wedge that sits low on the head, pointed front and back, with a folded curtain seam along the lower edge. No peak.

gloves

Plain fabric work gloves, a pair, centred on each hand. Free-drawn against the reference body's grip anchor — small and loose enough that the same shape covers either body's hand.

hair_bun

Pulled back sleek to a round bun behind the crown.

hair_long

Long. A wide sheet falls behind the body past the shoulders; a solid cap over the scalp and a panel down each side beside the face.

hair_short

A short crop. A solid cap over the scalp coming down just past the temples.

hair_swept

Swept back and up, taller and further out on the near side.

harness

A pair of load-bearing straps crossing the chest in an X, near shoulder to far hip and back, with a small ring where they cross. Free-drawn against the reference body — a loose fit, not a skin-tight one, so it reads the same on either body.

hat

A stiff peaked cap: the same snug dome as cap.json, plus a flat brim detail projecting over the brow.

helmet

A sealed helmet: one dome-shaped shell enclosing the whole head with real clearance (so it hides hair of any length instead of needing a special case to suppress it), with a genuine face-shaped opening cut into the polygon itself - not a tinted overlay, an actual hole, so the real face shows through. A thin glass bezel rings the opening for a visor read.

hi_vis_tabard

A bright safety tabard, open at the sides, worn over a shirt with two reflective stripes. Same shoulder-arc and side-curve fit as vest, cropped a little shorter and left open wider at the sides.

hood

A soft hood, up: a bulk drape behind the head and shoulders, plus a front edge that falls low enough to shade the brow. Same under/over head split as hair, so the skull hides the back and only the shadowed front shows.

jacket

A light open jacket worn unbuttoned over a top, hanging open down the front and reaching past the hip. Each front panel's shoulder and outer seam are the wearer's own shoulder-arc and side curves, so the seams sit right no matter the body; the open front edge and short cap sleeves are free-drawn.

knee_pads

A pair of strapped knee pads, one per leg, centred on each knee. Free-drawn against the reference body's knee anchors.

long_coat

A long open coat, hanging unbuttoned down to near the ankle. Same fitted shoulder/side seams and cap sleeves as jacket, just with the hem dropped to a duster length.

long_coat_closed

A long coat buttoned closed down the centre - the two front panels meet on the midline (no open lap), same fitted shoulder/side seams and cap sleeves as long_coat, hem at mid-shin.

mask

A surgical mask over the nose and mouth, tied behind the ears. Free-drawn between the brow and chin, small enough to read the same on either body.

med_cross

A red medical cross on the left breast - the medic's mark. One free-drawn plus, small enough to sit fine on either body.

pants

Plain denim trousers, an alternative to the skirt. A hip panel plus a fitted tube down each leg to the ankle. Each tube's top is the leg's own dome, so it swings with the leg exactly as the bare leg does; the hip panel is drawn last and reaches wide enough to stay over the tube tops through the whole stride.

pen_array

A three-pen array in the breast pocket - red, cyan, gold. The researcher's tell. Free-drawn, either body.

plates

Three overlapping armor plates strapped across the chest, worn over a shirt or harness. Free-drawn, small enough to read the same on either body.

satchel

A worn leather shoulder bag on a cross-body strap: the strap runs from the far shoulder down across the chest to rest against the near hip, where the bag itself hangs. Free-drawn against the reference body — it hangs clear of the skin rather than fitting it, so the same shape reads fine on either body.

scrub_cap

A loose tie-back scrub cap: the same silhouette as cap.json/hair_short scaled up a little for a poofier fit, plus a thin tie-band across the forehead.

shoes

Low leather slip-on shoes, a pair. Each shoe is the wearer's own foot outline, taken a little larger, so it always encloses the foot with no heel or toe poking out.

skirt

A short flared skirt in plain cloth. Sits on the low-waist line — that edge is the wearer's own — and flares out to a hem at mid-thigh. No leg openings, so it drapes over any lower body.

stand_collar

A stiff stand collar: a trapezoid band rising from the chest to the base of the neck, flaring wider at the top. Free-drawn, reads the same on either body.

star

A five-point star badge worn on the left breast - same placement and scale as badge.json, a different shape for a different office.

tank_top

A plain ribbed knit tank top. Every edge except the hem is one of the wearer's own curves: side seams from the torso sides, the shoulder line from the shoulder arc, the neckline from the neck hole. Fits any body it is drawn on.

tool_belt

A leather work belt like belt.json, hung with two tool pouches and a loop. Same waistline/low-waist fit, so it sits flush at the natural waist on any body.

vest

A close, sleeveless vest worn over a shirt, closed to a narrow gap down the front and ending at the waist. Each panel's shoulder and outer seam are the wearer's own shoulder-arc and side curves, same fitting as jacket, just closed up and cropped shorter.

visor

A slim visor band across the eyes - a single flat panel, worn on its own (no helmet) or read as a tinted lens. Recoloured per kit via items/visor_*.json.
